title_en: ID verification giant IDScan confirms data breach with more than 150 million driver’s licenses stolen
title_fa: ID verification giant IDScan confirms data breach with more than 150 million driver’s licenses stolen
excerpt_en: The ID checking company said the data breach included people's full names and driver's licenses and other government-issued identity documents.
excerpt_fa: شرکت بررسی شناسه گفت که نقض اطلاعات شامل نام کامل افراد و گواهینامه رانندگی و سایر اسناد هویتی صادر شده توسط دولت است.
content_en:
ID verification service IDScan has confirmed that a data breach involved the theft of driver’s licenses from its systems, a week after a report said the identity document checker had been breached during a year-long hack.
The company said in a website notice that hackers stole the driver’s licenses from the company’s cloud; the stolen information includes people’s full names and driver’s license numbers, along with identity numbers from other government-issued documents, such as passports.
The Louisiana-based firm is used by corporate customers from entertainment venues to cannabis dispensaries to check and verify the identity documents of their customers. The notice is the company’s first acknowledgement that it had been hacked. The company said last week that it was investigating an incident, but had not yet confirmed an intrusion.
IDScan said in its notice that it “received information” on or around September 1 about a claim of a hack, on the same day that independent cybersecurity journalist Brian Krebs first reported a data breach at IDScan.
Krebs reported that he was alerted to a website on the dark web that allowed anyone to search the driver’s license information of over 150 million people living in the United States and Canada, including accessing their photos. Krebs verified the authenticity of the data by examining his own record. The database also contained high-profile individuals, including the U.S. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, and a security researcher who also verified his data for Krebs’ report.
The Pentagon told TechCrunch last week that it was aware of the suspected breach, and a spokesperson for the FBI said it was also investigating the incident.
IDScan said on its website its investigation was ongoing. The company’s statement said that, “though full access to the information required payment” — likely referring to a demand for money made by the hackers to access the full cache of stolen data — the company was providing notice on its website to notify potentially affected individuals. IDScan has not said how many individuals are affected but notes on its website that it holds over 150 million driver’s license records.
IDScan did not respond to TechCrunch’s request for comment about the incident, such as whether the hackers contacted the company with a ransom demand not to release the data.
content_fa:
سرویس تأیید هویت IDScan تأیید کرده است که نقض داده‌ها شامل سرقت گواهینامه‌های رانندگی از سیستم‌هایش می‌شود، یک هفته پس از گزارشی مبنی بر اینکه بررسی‌کننده اسناد هویتی طی یک هک یک ساله نقض شده است.
این شرکت در اطلاعیه وب سایتی اعلام کرد که هکرها گواهینامه رانندگی را از فضای ابری شرکت دزدیده اند. اطلاعات دزدیده شده شامل نام کامل افراد و شماره گواهینامه رانندگی به همراه شماره هویت سایر اسناد صادر شده توسط دولت مانند گذرنامه است.
این شرکت مستقر در لوئیزیانا توسط مشتریان شرکتی از مکان های تفریحی گرفته تا داروخانه های شاهدانه برای بررسی و تأیید مدارک هویتی مشتریان خود استفاده می شود. این اطلاعیه اولین تایید شرکت مبنی بر هک شدن آن است. این شرکت هفته گذشته گفت که در حال بررسی یک حادثه است، اما هنوز نفوذی را تایید نکرده است.
IDScan در اطلاعیه خود گفت که در تاریخ 1 سپتامبر یا حوالی آن "اطلاعاتی" در مورد ادعای هک دریافت کرده است، در همان روزی که برایان کربس، روزنامه نگار مستقل امنیت سایبری برای اولین بار گزارش نقض داده در IDScan را گزارش کرد.
کربس گزارش داد که یک وب سایت در وب تاریک به او هشدار داده شده است که به هر کسی اجازه می دهد اطلاعات گواهینامه رانندگی بیش از 150 میلیون نفر را که در ایالات متحده و کانادا زندگی می کنند، از جمله دسترسی به عکس های آنها جستجو کند. کربس با بررسی سوابق خود صحت داده ها را تأیید کرد. این پایگاه داده همچنین حاوی افراد سرشناس از جمله وزیر دفاع ایالات متحده پیت هگست و یک محقق امنیتی بود که همچنین داده های او را برای گزارش کربس تأیید کرد.
پنتاگون هفته گذشته به TechCrunch گفت که از نقض مشکوک آگاه است و سخنگوی FBI نیز گفت که در حال بررسی این حادثه است.
IDScan در وب سایت خود اعلام کرد که تحقیقات آن ادامه دارد. در بیانیه این شرکت آمده است که «اگرچه دسترسی کامل به اطلاعات مورد نیاز پرداخت است» - احتمالاً به درخواست پولی که هکرها برای دسترسی به حافظه پنهان کامل داده‌های دزدیده شده اشاره می‌کند، این شرکت در وب‌سایت خود اطلاعیه‌ای را برای اطلاع دادن به افراد احتمالی تحت تأثیر قرار می‌دهد. IDScan نگفته است که چه تعداد از افراد تحت تأثیر قرار گرفته اند، اما در وب سایت خود اشاره می کند که بیش از 150 میلیون پرونده گواهینامه رانندگی دارد.
IDScan به درخواست TechCrunch برای اظهار نظر در مورد این حادثه پاسخ نداد، مانند اینکه آیا هکرها با این شرکت تماس گرفتند و درخواست باج دادند تا داده ها را منتشر نکنند.

title_en: Snapchat takes aim at Partiful with new event-planning features
title_fa: Snapchat با ویژگی های جدید برنامه ریزی رویداد، Partiful را هدف قرار می دهد
excerpt_en: Snapchat says the new features can be used to organize everything from birthday celebrations and sporting events to study sessions and weekend hangouts.
excerpt_fa: اسنپ ​​چت می گوید که از ویژگی های جدید می توان برای سازماندهی همه چیز از جشن تولد و رویدادهای ورزشی گرفته تا جلسات مطالعه و پاتوق های آخر هفته استفاده کرد.
content_en:
Snapchat announced on Thursday that it’s launching “Snapchat Plans,” a suite of features for creating, sharing, and managing real-world events with friends. The new event-planning features allow users to send and receive invitations and track details like the time, location, and attendees, all in one place.
Snapchat says the new features can be used to organize everything from birthday celebrations and sporting events to study sessions and weekend hangouts.
With Snapchat Plans, the social network is looking to take on Partiful, a popular event planning and digital invitation platform, as young users turn to dedicated apps to organize get-togethers rather than relying on group chats or social media. Snapchat isn’t the only tech company taking on Partiful and other invitation apps, as Apple launched an app called Invites last year that lets users create custom invitations for any occasion.
Snapchat users can create an event, called a “Snapchat Plan,” by adding a title, choosing a date and time, and inviting up to 200 friends. Invitations are then delivered directly within a one-on-one chat with each invited friend. Guests can then RSVP with “Going,” “Maybe,” or “Can’t Go.”
The app is also adding a new “My Plans” section on users’ profiles that lets them quickly browse all of their current, upcoming, and past Snapchat Plans. Additionally, once users click on a friend’s profile, they will see the events they share with them.
Once a Snapchat Plan is created, hosts can see who’s attending, invite more friends, and update event details as needed. Guests can view the full guest list, change their RSVP at any time, and get a reminder one hour before the event starts.
Although Snapchat has been a significant player in the social media space over the past decade, the company is now expanding its focus beyond how people communicate online to also help shape how they get together in the real world. This follows the broader trend that sees Gen Z looking for more in-person connections.
“No more missed get-togethers because of buried messages, lost details, or forgetting to create an invitation,” the company wrote in a blog post. “Snapchat Plans make it easier to organize these special in-person moments with your friends.”
Snapchat Plans are private and invite-only, the company says.
content_fa:
اسنپ ​​چت روز پنجشنبه اعلام کرد که "Snapchat Plans" را راه اندازی می کند، مجموعه ای از ویژگی ها برای ایجاد، اشتراک گذاری و مدیریت رویدادهای دنیای واقعی با دوستان. ویژگی های جدید برنامه ریزی رویداد به کاربران امکان می دهد دعوت نامه ها را ارسال و دریافت کنند و جزئیاتی مانند زمان، مکان و شرکت کنندگان را در یک مکان پیگیری کنند.
اسنپ ​​چت می گوید که از ویژگی های جدید می توان برای سازماندهی همه چیز از جشن تولد و رویدادهای ورزشی گرفته تا جلسات مطالعه و پاتوق های آخر هفته استفاده کرد.
با برنامه‌های اسنپ چت، این شبکه اجتماعی به دنبال پذیرش Partiful است، یک پلتفرم محبوب برنامه‌ریزی رویداد و دعوت دیجیتال، زیرا کاربران جوان به جای تکیه بر چت‌های گروهی یا رسانه‌های اجتماعی، به برنامه‌های اختصاصی برای سازمان‌دهی گردهمایی‌ها روی می‌آورند. اسنپ ​​چت تنها شرکت فناوری نیست که برنامه های Partiful و سایر برنامه های دعوت را انجام می دهد، زیرا اپل سال گذشته اپلیکیشنی به نام Invites را راه اندازی کرد که به کاربران امکان می دهد برای هر مناسبتی دعوت نامه های سفارشی ایجاد کنند.
کاربران اسنپ چت می توانند با افزودن عنوان، انتخاب تاریخ و زمان و دعوت از 200 دوست، رویدادی به نام «طرح اسنپ چت» ایجاد کنند. سپس دعوت‌نامه‌ها مستقیماً در یک چت یک به یک با هر دوست دعوت شده ارسال می‌شوند. سپس میهمانان می‌توانند با «رفتن»، «شاید» یا «نمی‌توانم بروم» پاسخ دهند.
این برنامه همچنین در حال افزودن بخش جدیدی به نام «برنامه‌های من» در نمایه‌های کاربران است که به آن‌ها اجازه می‌دهد به سرعت تمام برنامه‌های اسنپ‌چت فعلی، آینده و گذشته خود را مرور کنند. علاوه بر این، هنگامی که کاربران روی نمایه یک دوست کلیک کنند، رویدادهایی را که با آنها به اشتراک می گذارند مشاهده خواهند کرد.
پس از ایجاد طرح اسنپ چت، میزبان ها می توانند ببینند چه کسانی شرکت می کنند، دوستان بیشتری را دعوت کنند و جزئیات رویداد را در صورت نیاز به روز کنند. مهمانان می‌توانند فهرست کامل مهمانان را مشاهده کنند، پاسخ‌های پاسخ خود را در هر زمان تغییر دهند و یک ساعت قبل از شروع رویداد یادآوری دریافت کنند.
اگرچه اسنپ چت در دهه گذشته بازیگر مهمی در فضای رسانه های اجتماعی بوده است، اما این شرکت اکنون تمرکز خود را فراتر از نحوه برقراری ارتباط آنلاین افراد گسترش می دهد تا به شکل گیری نحوه گردهمایی آنها در دنیای واقعی نیز کمک کند. این روند گسترده‌تری را دنبال می‌کند که ژنرال Z به دنبال ارتباطات حضوری بیشتری است.
این شرکت در یک پست وبلاگی نوشت: «دیگر به دلیل پیام‌های مدفون، جزئیات از دست رفته یا فراموش کردن ایجاد دعوتنامه، گردهمایی از دست رفته نیست. "برنامه های اسنپ چت سازماندهی این لحظات ویژه حضوری با دوستانتان را آسان تر می کند."
این شرکت می‌گوید، برنامه‌های اسنپ‌چت خصوصی و فقط دعوت‌شده هستند.

title_en: Insta360 Luna Pro review: Your Instagram Reels are about to get an upgrade
title_fa: بررسی Insta360 Luna Pro: قرقره های اینستاگرام شما در شرف ارتقا هستند
excerpt_en: There's now a direct rival to the Osmo Pocket 4 you can easily buy in the US.
excerpt_fa: There's now a direct rival to the Osmo Pocket 4 you can easily buy in the US.
content_en:
Insta360 Luna Pro review: Your Instagram Reels are about to get an upgrade
There’s now a direct rival to the Osmo Pocket 4 you can easily buy in the US.
It's been a bumper summer for pocketable cameras. DJI kicked off the season with the Pocket 4, a much anticipated follow-up to the wildly popular Pocket 3. But that was just the warm up. Then came Insta360's Luna Ultra, with a dual-lens/optical zoom setup. This was swiftly answered by DJI with the Pocket 4P, formally establishing a "pro" tier to the gimbal-camera category. In between all that, GoPro delivered the Mission 1 Pro, twice, and both DJI and Insta360 unveiled rugged 360 cams. Today, we can add one more to that list: the Insta360 Luna Pro ($600).
On paper, it's the company's response to the Pocket 4 — a single lens, 20mm fixed focal length gimbal camera. That might not sound like a rousing finale to the pocket-camera bonanza, but Insta360 is smart and saved a few tricks for the Pro version that at least make it a solid encore. If you create for Instagram Reels, TikTok or YouTube Shorts, it might even be the most interesting pick of the pack.
Hardware
From the neck down, the Luna Pro is almost identical to the Ultra. The only visual difference is the wider frame along the top edge of the display with the word "Luna" printed in cursive. Above the collar, it's a different story, with a smaller, single-lens gimbal head that shaves about half an inch off the total height of the device. The Luna Pro also comes with the same pop-off front panel that doubles as a wireless remote and microphone.
Internally, the Pro matches the specs of the Luna Ultra's main 20mm camera. That means the same Leica Summicron lens (f1.8/20mm) paired with a 1-inch sensor that supports 8K/30 and 4K/120. Dolby Vision, 10-bit I-Log and 37-megapixel photos are all here, too. One notable difference in the Pro's favor (at the time of writing) is support for true 4K shooting in 9:16 mode (screen in portrait). The Luna Ultra, like the Pocket 4 and 4P, currently only offers 3K in portrait mode. So on the Pro, there's no more holding the camera horizontally for true 4K, social media-friendly videos.
The Luna Pro also has the same 47GB of internal storage, expandable via SD card and the same 1,550 mAh battery as the Ultra. The near identical dimensions of the body mean accessories should be largely compatible unless it's something that attaches to the gimbal head. For example, Insta360 provided a fill-light accessory for this review, which connects to the collar of the gimbal mechanism, so it's not compatible with the Luna Ultra. Fun fact, you can swap the detachable displays between models, and they will still work — even wirelessly — but the screen will update its firmware to match the new camera each time. When I tried this, I lost the 4K portrait menu option on the Pro, which meant I needed a factory reset to resolve the problem. It's something you can do, but probably shouldn't.
Video quality
Like the Luna Ultra before it, the Pro reliably delivers a crisp, high-quality image. In 4K, colors are bright and appear gently saturated to give them a confident pop. The f1.8 aperture provides good depth and subject separation without being over dramatic. I found the Luna Pro gives just a dash more bokeh compared to the Osmo Pocket 4 under the same conditions with close up subjects, although DJI's camera has a richer color depth to my eye.
Both the Luna Pro and the Pocket 4 are very close in terms of image quality, but in casual testing on default settings, the Luna Pro's detail and blacks are a little more punchy. Like the Osmo Pocket, the Luna Pro has full i-Log recording with color restoration for tuning the image to your style or preference. The Luna also supports Dolby Vision.
I used the Luna Pro as my main B-roll camera for this review video of the new GoPro and was surprised at how well it handled a variety of lighting situations. Moving between dark and well lit areas is generally smooth, but sometimes the transition of exposure isn't subtle. If there's one slight weak spot, bright backgrounds or sunny, overcast skies occasionally over expose in standard color mode when there's a wide dynamic range. Use I-Log and you usually have enough headroom to tame them.
Despite the obvious focus on video, the photos for Engadget's Mission 1 Pro ILS review were taken with the Luna Pro. I wouldn't go as far to suggest it can be your main camera for stills, but for a video-first camera I was impressed enough with the results to use them for publication.
4K and 4x
At launch, the Luna Pro has a feature not found on any of the gimbal cameras we've talked about so far: native 4K in portrait mode. Until now, the minute you flick the screen to shoot in 9:16 on a DJI or Insta Luna Ultra, the max resolution drops to 3K. There are some technical reasons for this, but it was particularly frustrating on the Luna Ultra, given it has an 8K sensor (and presumably more headroom for vertical video). Well, the Pro casually does 4K/30 in portrait mode, like it's no biggie.
There are still some limitations. For one, 4K in portrait mode tops out at 30 fps, while in landscape mode you can go right up to 120 fps. If you drop back down to 3K, you can increase this to 60 fps. You can, of course, still hold the Luna Pro at 90-degrees and have all the features the camera offers, but you lose one axis of gimbal stabilization, and it's less natural filming that way.
Insta360 claims the Luna Pro has "HiRes" 4x zoom, despite just the one lens. For 2x zoom, you're still within the 8K sensor's native shot, but once you go beyond that, software is enhancing things behind the scenes. This is how the Pocket 4 also works. Insta360 Luna Pro review: Your Instagram Reels are about to get an upgrade
There’s now a direct rival to the Osmo Pocket 4 you can easily buy in the US.
It's been a bumper summer for pocketable cameras. DJI kicked off the season with the Pocket 4, a much anticipated follow-up to the wildly popular Pocket 3. But that was just the warm up. Then came Insta360's Luna Ultra, with a dual-lens/optical zoom setup. This was swiftly answered by DJI with the Pocket 4P, formally establishing a "pro" tier to the gimbal-camera category. In between all that, GoPro delivered the Mission 1 Pro, twice, and both DJI and Insta360 unveiled rugged 360 cams. Today, we can add one more to that list: the Insta360 Luna Pro ($600).
On paper, it's the company's response to the Pocket 4 — a single lens, 20mm fixed focal length gimbal camera. That might not sound like a rousing finale to the pocket-camera bonanza, but Insta360 is smart and saved a few tricks for the Pro version that at least make it a solid encore. If you create for Instagram Reels, TikTok or YouTube Shorts, it might even be the most interesting pick of the pack.
Hardware
From the neck down, the Luna Pro is almost identical to the Ultra. The only visual difference is the wider frame along the top edge of the display with the word "Luna" printed in cursive. Above the collar, it's a different story, with a smaller, single-lens gimbal head that shaves about half an inch off the total height of the device. The Luna Pro also comes with the same pop-off front panel that doubles as a wireless remote and microphone.
Internally, the Pro matches the specs of the Luna Ultra's main 20mm camera. That means the same Leica Summicron lens (f1.8/20mm) paired with a 1-inch sensor that supports 8K/30 and 4K/120. Dolby Vision, 10-bit I-Log and 37-megapixel photos are all here, too. One notable difference in the Pro's favor (at the time of writing) is support for true 4K shooting in 9:16 mode (screen in portrait). The Luna Ultra, like the Pocket 4 and 4P, currently only offers 3K in portrait mode. So on the Pro, there's no more holding the camera horizontally for true 4K, social media-friendly videos.
The Luna Pro also has the same 47GB of internal storage, expandable via SD card and the same 1,550 mAh battery as the Ultra. The near identical dimensions of the body mean accessories should be largely compatible unless it's something that attaches to the gimbal head. For example, Insta360 provided a fill-light accessory for this review, which connects to the collar of the gimbal mechanism, so it's not compatible with the Luna Ultra. Fun fact, you can swap the detachable displays between models, and they will still work — even wirelessly — but the screen will update its firmware to match the new camera each time. When I tried this, I lost the 4K portrait menu option on the Pro, which meant I needed a factory reset to resolve the problem. It's something you can do, but probably shouldn't.
Video quality
Like the Luna Ultra before it, the Pro reliably delivers a crisp, high-quality image. In 4K, colors are bright and appear gently saturated to give them a confident pop. The f1.8 aperture provides good depth and subject separation without being over dramatic. I found the Luna Pro gives just a dash more bokeh compared to the Osmo Pocket 4 under the same conditions with close up subjects, although DJI's camera has a richer color depth to my eye.
Both the Luna Pro and the Pocket 4 are very close in terms of image quality, but in casual testing on default settings, the Luna Pro's detail and blacks are a little more punchy. Like the Osmo Pocket, the Luna Pro has full i-Log recording with color restoration for tuning the image to your style or preference. The Luna also supports Dolby Vision.
I used the Luna Pro as my main B-roll camera for this review video of the new GoPro and was surprised at how well it handled a variety of lighting situations. Moving between dark and well lit areas is generally smooth, but sometimes the transition of exposure isn't subtle. If there's one slight weak spot, bright backgrounds or sunny, overcast skies occasionally over expose in standard color mode when there's a wide dynamic range. Use I-Log and you usually have enough headroom to tame them.
Despite the obvious focus on video, the photos for Engadget's Mission 1 Pro ILS review were taken with the Luna Pro. I wouldn't go as far to suggest it can be your main camera for stills, but for a video-first camera I was impressed enough with the results to use them for publication.
4K and 4x
At launch, the Luna Pro has a feature not found on any of the gimbal cameras we've talked about so far: native 4K in portrait mode. Until now, the minute you flick the screen to shoot in 9:16 on a DJI or Insta Luna Ultra, the max resolution drops to 3K. There are some technical reasons for this, but it was particularly frustrating on the Luna Ultra, given it has an 8K sensor (and presumably more headroom for vertical video). Well, the Pro casually does 4K/30 in portrait mode, like it's no biggie.
There are still some limitations. For one, 4K in portrait mode tops out at 30 fps, while in landscape mode you can go right up to 120 fps. If you drop back down to 3K, you can increase this to 60 fps. You can, of course, still hold the Luna Pro at 90-degrees and have all the features the camera offers, but you lose one axis of gimbal stabilization, and it's less natural filming that way.

title_en: You can now plan IRL events on Snapchat
title_fa: You can now plan IRL events on Snapchat
excerpt_en: Snapchat Plans lets you organize IRL gatherings, though it's missing one seemingly obvious detail.
excerpt_fa: برنامه‌های اسنپ چت به شما امکان می‌دهد گردهمایی‌های IRL را سازماندهی کنید، اگرچه یک جزئیات به ظاهر واضح را از دست داده است.
content_en:
You can now plan IRL events on Snapchat
What's old is new.
Snapchat is getting a very old-school social media feature: event planning. Called "Snapchat Plans" the app is trying to foster IRL gatherings of its users with new tools to organize meetups of up to 200 people directly in the app.
According to Snap, more than a third of its core users are already using the app's group chats to plan get-togethers. Plans creates a dedicated space for organizing events and tracking invites. Users can access the feature from the "My Plans" section of their profile. When a new event is created, Snapchat will deliver invites via DMs in chat and people can RSVP with the typical "going," "can't go" or maybe. There are also a few Snapchat-specific elements, like Bitmoji-themed cover art.
According to Snap, all events are private and only visible to their creator and invitees, though anyone invited can view the guest list. Strangely, the feature doesn't appear to include the ability to add location details, even though the app has a widely-used map feature. A spokesperson tells Engadget the company is "actively working on" the ability to add location info to Plans, though it's unclear if it will utilize the Snap Map in some way.
There's something a little amusing about Snapchat, which has repeatedly claimed it's "not social media," adding a mundane social feature like events. It's even more amusing that the feature doesn't include location info which, I don't know, seems like a pretty crucial aspect to planning something IRL! But maybe the company knows something I don't about how Gen Z makes plans. Actually, it's a pretty safe bet that they do.

title_en: Apple Watch Series 12 hands-on: New sensing system, health features and audio intelligence
title_fa: Apple Watch Series 12 hands-on: New sensing system, health features and audio intelligence
excerpt_en: There was a lot more new stuff than expected.
excerpt_fa: There was a lot more new stuff than expected.
content_en:
Apple Watch Series 12 hands-on: New sensing system, health features and audio intelligence
There was a lot more new stuff than expected.
I wasn't expecting Apple to have a ton of interesting updates to the Apple Watch this year, but somehow it managed to surprise me. Some of the new features coming to the Apple Watch Series 12 are things the competition has already offered, like Readiness scores and increased sampling rates. But others, like the Audio Intelligence suite of tools and even the new finishes and materials, are novel. I'm also not against AI wearables that listen to your surroundings and conversations, as long as done responsibly and with accountability, so I'm intrigued by things like Siri Recap and Live Rewind.
Unfortunately, I wasn't really able to test out most of these features at the demo area right after the "Surprise and shine" keynote ended. But I did get to spend a bit more time with some Apple Watch demos, and carefully scrutinize what exactly is different on the Series 12. I also got a bit more detail on how the new Audio Intelligence features work and whether Apple is listening to your conversations. (Short answer: No.)
One of the main changes in the Apple Watch Series 12 is in the sensing system, which Apple says it has re-architected. I actually got to compare my Series 11 to the new smartwatch, and their undersides certainly look quite different. I could go into greater detail on how the photodiodes and the LEDs have been upgraded and rearranged, but suffice to say that on the newer model, you'll notice a ring of 12 lights compared to the four LEDs laid out in a diamond shape on last year's device.
New health sensing system on the Apple Watch Series 12
If you look really close, you'll notice differences in other components as well, like the number and layout of the diodes and electrodes around the LEDs. With the increased surface area that's in contact with your skin, the updated hardware should lead to more accurate and consistent readings. Apple is also increasing its sampling rates so it's getting measurements of your heart rate (and therefore related data like your VO2Max and heart rate variability) much more frequently. Apple goes as far as to say that it conducted its own study of wearables and found the Series 12 to be the most accurate in heart rate sensing.
That data feeds into a few health-related features on the Apple Watch Series 12, including the updated heart rate app, which has a new HRV metric. That's now measured at up to every five minutes, compared to every two to four hours or so on older watches.
The HRV information is a key part of the new Readiness app on the watch, and factors into your readiness score each day. This is delivered daily on a scale of 0 to 10, and takes into account your activity, sleep and vitals. Of course, I wasn't able to test this myself as I'd have to wear an Apple Watch for at least seven days for it to work. But the number I did see on a company rep's watch was a concerning "3," and upon closer investigation the Health app said that poor sleep and HRV performance brought the score down.
Apple also made some tweaks to the Vitals app, changing up some of the language it uses around performance. But the biggest update to the Apple Watch experience might be outside of the watch itself. The Health app is getting quite a significant makeover, which might sound like welcome news to longtime users who never quite enjoyed how to make sense of their data in that app.
Since Apple Intelligence summaries are part of the redesigned Health app, you'll have to have a compatible iPhone to use it. (If not, you'll see the current version.) This updated version is coming later this year, with the first thing you see being a summary generated by Apple Intelligence at the top. This considers the time of day to deliver your most relevant information at the time. Then come tiles that show your metrics like activity, heart and sleep, and these will also change order throughout the day.
Swiping sideways on the home screen will take you through sleep, fitness and heart pages, while the bottom navigation bar shows you options to go into the Longevity and data tabs. The Longevity tab is a new interface that not only measures your wellbeing across seven different areas including the ones I already mentioned, but also shows your "health age." It's a bit confusing to me all the different names for what I think should be the same thing, but I'm sure after I spend some time with the app later this year I'll understand the distinctions better. I'm also intrigued and keen to try out some of the new assessments in the app, like the one for VO2Max where you'll have to follow along instructions to jog in place, while the Health app studies your heart rate from your Apple Watch or compatible AirPods to evaluate your performance.
While the refreshed Health app isn't going to be available for a while, nor is it exclusive to the Apple Watch Series 12, it certainly impacts a lot of your experience. It is where you'll spend a lot of time looking at your health data, after all. But more features coming to the Series 12 are around AI, performance and "audio intelligence."
Audio Intelligence, AI and privacy concerns on the Apple Watch Series 12
One thing that's important to keep in mind when thinking about the new Apple Watch's sound and listening-related features is the S11 chip. It's designed with what Apple calls the "secure exclave," which is where the raw audio coming in from the watch's microphone is being processed. That's where the sound is transcribed and processed, and only the results of that interpretation leave the exclave. It won't store any of the audio it gets, Apple says.
With this, there are four updates related to sound. First up is the most straightforward: Improvements to Shazam on your watch. Right now, if you want to pull up Shazam to identify a song playing around you, you might scroll through the smart stack on your watch and whizz...

title_en: NASA and IBM made an AI model for exploring the Moon
title_fa: NASA and IBM made an AI model for exploring the Moon
excerpt_en: NASA and IBM's latest collaboration is an AI model of the moon made for the Artemis era.
excerpt_fa: آخرین همکاری ناسا و IBM یک مدل هوش مصنوعی از ماه است که برای دوران آرتمیس ساخته شده است.
content_en:
NASA and IBM made an AI model for exploring the Moon
The two organizations are also releasing a dataset researchers can use to make their own models.
This past spring, the world experienced a rare moment of collective joy and awe when NASA's Artemis II mission, the first crewed flight to the Moon since 1972, completed its historic lunar flyby. On April 6, astronauts Reid Wiseman, Christina Koch, Victor Glover and Jeremy Hansen flew farther from Earth than any humans before them. Now, as NASA prepares for the next Artemis mission and beyond, the space agency is working with IBM to give scientists new tools to study the Moon.
On Thursday, the two organizations released the NASA-IBM Lunar Foundation Model. It's an open-source AI system that's available to download from Hugging Face. As a foundation model, it can do a few different things, says Dr. Juan Bernabé-Moreno, the director of IBM Research Europe, UK and Ireland. To start, NASA and IBM found it was particularly adept at identifying areas on the lunar surface where there might be ice.
The two organizations ran a test where they compared the model's predictions against a map they made using a published scientific workflow that incorporates terrain, thermal and other environmental data. They then pitted the model against SwinV2-B, a Microsoft-trained vision system for processing high-resolution images. The NASA-IBM model reduced errors by 23 percent. NASA and IBM compared the model against SwinV2-B because the tool is often used as the baseline for many image analysis tasks.
NASA and IBM also benchmarked their model's ability to identify and classify craters. There, the new model outperformed SwinV2-B by 19 percent while using half the training data. NASA and IBM got a chance to verify the model's capabilities recently when a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket crashed into the Moon on August 5. When IBM fed an image of the impact to the model, it correctly identified the crash site as a new crater, despite it closely overlapping with an existing crater. "It worked fantastically," says Bernabé-Moreno, with the model nailing the identification on its first attempt.
Bernabé-Moreno says training the model was a challenge. "In Earth observation, you have pristine images," he explains. Our planet's atmosphere scatters sunlight, filling shadows with ambient light that softens their edges. Shadows on the Moon instead appear knife-edged and pitch black, meaning any time they're photographed, the shadowed pixels don't carry any information. "On the Moon, what you have is the sun at different moments during the day, and it illuminates and it cuts shadows, and you need to deal with those shadows," he says. The result is that a crater can look one way in one image and completely different in the next image.
Another challenge came as a result of how computer vision models are typically trained and tested. Most often, that process involves removing some parts of an image and then tasking the model with reconstructing what's missing based on the patterns it has learned in training. "You might remove 90 percent of a crater, and with [the remaining] 10 percent, you ask the model to reconstruct the other 90 percent," explains Bernabé-Moreno. That doesn't work for the Moon. As you might imagine, the reason for that is that a lot of craters look very similar to one another when photographed from orbit.
In fact, IBM's attempts to train the model in the traditional way were a "complete disaster," says Bernabé-Moreno, but the research team eventually devised a creative solution. "We took the Moon and divided it into wedges, like an orange, and we completely separated the training wedges from the testing wedges. This way, we could give the model a lot of consistency," he says.
One of the reasons NASA and IBM are excited about this release is that it includes a first-of-its-kind open-source dataset that other researchers can use to build future models. It incorporates tens of thousands of images and instrument data from NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) and Gravity Recovery and Interior Laboratory (GRAIL) missions, as well as Japan's Selenological and Engineering Explorer (SELENE).
"One of the reasons we've never seen a comprehensive, powerful lunar model before is that we didn't have the data [organized] in the right way," says Bernabé-Moreno. Organization in this case meant creating a grid where every pixel of imaging data corresponds to other modalities of data a model can use to inform its processing. "That alone is a massive scientific contribution, because put the model aside: the community now has a co-registered dataset with more than two million [data] points," says Bernabé-Moreno. "And we know that AI models get superseded by other models. The data is what really creates the industry of AI models."

title_en: iOS 27 brings GymKit to iPhone and AirPods, but what does it actually do?
title_fa: iOS 27 brings GymKit to iPhone and AirPods, but what does it actually do?
excerpt_en: GymKit is a great idea that has never been fully realized. Now, it doesn't require an Apple Watch to take advantage of.
excerpt_fa: GymKit is a great idea that has never been fully realized. Now, it doesn't require an Apple Watch to take advantage of.
content_en:
iOS 27 brings GymKit to iPhone and AirPods, but what does it actually do?
GymKit never became as popular as it should have, but great compatibility could fix that.
Released in October 2017, Apple's GymKit is an exciting idea that was never widely adopted. The premise is simple: you tap your watch to a machine in the gym to enable data syncing in both directions. The gym equipment can display what your watch is measuring, while your watch uses the machine's metrics to better calculate the quality of your workout. However, gym equipment replacement tends to be a slow process and purchasing equipment for the home is getting more expensive every year. Given the need for an Apple Watch and a compatible cardio machine, Apple's exercise API has had a lot working against it.
With iOS 27, however, Apple is bringing GymKit to iPhone. With this update, your AirPods Pro 3 will handle heart rate data, while the iPhone becomes the screen and record-keeper for workouts. The exercise machine completes the trifecta, contributing its own gathered workout information to the Fitness app.
Nothing has changed on the compatibility front. The cardio machine still needs Apple's GymKit integration, whether you're using an Apple Watch or an iPhone. iOS 27 just adds the same tap-to-connect option for iPhone, so you use the NFC reader with your phone instead of your watch.
Without GymKit integration, iPhones and AirPods are still useful for ordinary workout tracking. They just won't pull any data from the exercise equipment.
How iPhone and AirPods fit into GymKit
With iOS 27, the process of connecting with GymKit is the same as using your iPhone to pay at a store. With a compatible machine handy, tap the iPhone on the GymKit or NFC connection point, choose the type of workout and start the session. Treadmills, ellipticals, bikes and stair steppers are mentioned among the supported types of cardio equipment, but compatibility may extend to other units as well.
If you're wearing AirPods Pro 3, the earbuds will provide live heart rate data to your iPhone, which feeds that information to the equipment, which sends workout details to the Fitness app. It's all one big, clean circle of data. According to Apple's GymKit privacy page, the workout information is removed from the connected equipment once your workout session ends, unless you're using a machine you've signed into.
The point is that you no longer need an Apple Watch to take advantage of workout features that were once exclusive to the wearable. If you forget to charge your watch, you can still connect to compatible workout equipment with an iPhone and AirPods Pro 3.
What GymKit does and doesn't replace
Unfortunately, this new functionality is not a full-fledged replacement of the Apple Watch. Your iPhone and compatible AirPods supply all the data you could realistically need from a workout session. But the Apple Watch is a broader tool that provides the all-day, all-night data context to go along with daily workout routines.
There are practical limitations, too. You must have your iPhone updated to iOS 27, and need AirPods Pro 3 for heart rate tracking. As of this writing, GymKit-supported cardio machines will disconnect from an iPhone if AirPods Pro 3 aren't also in the mix. Perhaps the biggest obstacle is compatible workout equipment, since many of the machines common in gyms and home setups don't work with GymKit.
If you don't own an Apple Watch, tend to forget it at home or don't charge it on a regular basis, the iOS 27 update paired with AirPods Pro 3 will do the trick in a pinch. Due to the practical constraints of needing your phone and AirPods, though, wearing a charged and ready-to-go Apple Watch is still the more convenient option.

title_en: Trump Mobile's T1 Phone now costs $250 more
title_fa: Trump Mobile's T1 Phone now costs $250 more
excerpt_en: Trump Mobile's T1 Phone, which an iFixit teardown revealed to be pretty much identical to an HTC handset, got a $250 price hike.
excerpt_fa: Trump Mobile's T1 Phone, which an iFixit teardown revealed to be pretty much identical to an HTC handset, got a $250 price hike.
content_en:
Trump Mobile's T1 Phone now costs $250 more
You’ll have to pay $749 for a Trump phone.
Trump Mobile's golden T1 Phone now costs $749. That's a $250 price hike from $499, making the T1 more expensive than the iPhone 17e. The price hike was first reported by The Verge, which also noted that the provider didn't make an announcement about it and just quietly updated its website.
While Trump Mobile didn't explain why the T1 now costs a lot more, tech companies have been raising the prices of their products across the board recently due to skyrocketing costs of RAM. No one is safe from the RAMageddon, which is what people are calling the memory chip shortage problem currently plaguing the electronics industry due to massive AI buildouts. In fact, Apple just increased the prices of older iPhones by $100, almost three months after it raised the prices of iPads (by up to $200), MacBooks (by up to $500) and its Mac Studio computer (by up to $1,300).
In addition, the T1's price increase seems expected. Trump Mobile's execs previously said that the $499 price tag was just introductory and that buyers could be paying $999 for it in the future. Take note that an iFixit teardown had revealed that the phone isn't made in the US, which Trump Mobile initially claimed, and is pretty much a reskinned version of an HTC handset.

title_en: Volvo XC40 PHEV is back with a new look, better sensors, and Gemini AI
title_fa: Volvo XC40 PHEV با ظاهری جدید، حسگرهای بهتر و هوش مصنوعی Gemini بازگشته است
excerpt_en: It's been about three years since Volvo discontinued its plug-in hybrid XC40. The mild hybrid version remains on sale in the US and elsewhere, alongside the electric EX40. Today, Volvo announced it was bringing back the PHEV version and giving it a major facelift. When it...
excerpt_fa: حدود سه سال از زمانی که ولوو مدل هیبریدی پلاگین XC40 خود را متوقف کرد، می گذرد. نسخه هیبریدی ملایم در کنار EX40 الکتریکی در ایالات متحده و جاهای دیگر به فروش می رسد. امروز، ولوو اعلام کرد که نسخه PHEV را بازگردانده و فیس لیفت بزرگی به آن می دهد. وقتی آن ...
content_en:
It’s been about three years since Volvo discontinued its plug-in hybrid XC40. The mild hybrid version remains on sale in the US and elsewhere, alongside the electric EX40. Today, Volvo announced it was bringing back the PHEV version and giving it a major facelift. When it arrives at dealerships early next year, the new XC40 will have updated exterior styling, a gut-renovated interior featuring Google’s Gemini AI assistant, enlarged infotainment screen, and a new sensor-and-software safety suite.
Volvo XC40 PHEV is back with a new look, better sensors, and Gemini AI
The plug-in hybrid version of Volvo’s small SUV is making a comeback.
The plug-in hybrid version of Volvo’s small SUV is making a comeback.
As a hybrid, the XC40 serves as a bridge for customers who want better gas mileage but aren’t ready for the pure EV lifestyle. Volvo itself needs that bridge, after backing down from its pledge to sell only EVs by 2030. That said, the automaker didn’t divulge any details about the powertrain, engine options, electric motor, range, or battery capacity for the XC40 — so we’ll have to wait and see whether this SUV can sufficiently compete in an increasingly cutthroat hybrid market.
On the surface, we’ve got a new take on Volvo’s signature “Thor’s Hammer” LED headlights, as well as an updated front grille, bumper, hood and front wings. Same goes for the rear: new lighting, new bumper, and an upgraded tailgate. Additionally, the XC40 is getting a trio of diamond-cut wheel options, available in 18-, 19-, and 20-inch sizes.
But the interior is where the meat of Volvo’s improvements comes through. The screen has been bumped up to a higher resolution and a larger, 11.2-inch size. It will run Volvo’s latest user interface, which the automaker designed for faster navigation with fewer taps. Google’s Gemini serves as the voice assistant, using its big AI brain to plan routes, find specific locations and detours, and manage messages. The XC40 rounds it out with an improved wireless phone charger and smart storage solutions.
What about safety? This is a Volvo after all, the automaker most committed to Safety (at least according to its well-cultivated reputation). Don’t worry, the XC40 ups the ante in that department with a new software and sensor platform that’s designed to provide real-time collision avoidance, automated emergency steering, and automatic emergency braking.
The sensor upgrade includes new front and corner radars, a new front camera, new rear corner radars, 12 new ultrasonic sensors, and new parking cameras. Cloaked in this new sensor suite, the XC40 is getting a host of new safety capabilities, including new door opening alerts that warn occupants before dooring passing cyclists, lane change assist and smoother lane following support on long drives, and an optional 3D/360-degree camera to simplify low-speed maneuvering and parking.
The ultimate goal is to build a better XC40 — one that’s safer and more capable, which hopefully translates to better sales numbers and a long, continuous shelf life for Volvo’s tiny SUV.
“By enhancing the XC40’s design, technology and safety features, we’ve created the best version of the XC40 yet,” says Akhil Krishnan, Interim Lead for the 30 and 40 Series at Volvo Cars, in a statement. “This already popular model is now set to continue being one of our best-selling cars for years to come.”
Images by Volvo
content_fa:
حدود سه سال از توقف تولید هیبریدی پلاگین XC40 ولوو می گذرد. نسخه هیبریدی ملایم در کنار EX40 الکتریکی در ایالات متحده و جاهای دیگر به فروش می رسد. امروز، ولوو اعلام کرد که نسخه PHEV را بازگردانده و فیس لیفت بزرگی به آن می دهد. وقتی XC40 جدید در اوایل سال آینده وارد نمایندگی‌ها شود، ظاهر بیرونی به‌روز شده، فضای داخلی بازسازی‌شده با دستیار هوش مصنوعی Gemini گوگل، صفحه نمایش اطلاعات سرگرمی بزرگ‌شده و مجموعه‌ای از سنسورها و نرم‌افزارهای ایمنی جدید خواهد داشت.
Volvo XC40 PHEV با ظاهری جدید، حسگرهای بهتر و هوش مصنوعی Gemini بازگشته است
نسخه هیبریدی پلاگین شاسی بلند کوچک ولوو در حال بازگشت است.
نسخه هیبریدی پلاگین شاسی بلند کوچک ولوو در حال بازگشت است.
XC40 به‌عنوان یک هیبریدی، به‌عنوان پلی برای مشتریانی عمل می‌کند که می‌خواهند مسافت پیموده‌شده بنزین بهتری داشته باشند، اما برای سبک زندگی خالص EV آماده نیستند. خود ولوو پس از عقب نشینی از تعهد خود مبنی بر فروش تنها خودروهای برقی تا سال 2030 به این پل نیاز دارد. با این حال، خودروساز هیچ جزئیاتی در مورد پیشرانه، گزینه های موتور، موتور الکتریکی، برد یا ظرفیت باتری XC40 فاش نکرد – بنابراین باید منتظر بمانیم و ببینیم که آیا این SUV می تواند به اندازه کافی در بازار هیبریدی رقابت کند.
در ظاهر، ما برداشت جدیدی از چراغ‌های جلوی LED «Thor’s Hammer» ولوو و همچنین جلوپنجره جلو، سپر، کاپوت و بال‌های جلو به‌روز شده‌ایم. در قسمت عقب نیز همینطور است: نورپردازی جدید، سپر جدید و درب عقب ارتقا یافته. علاوه بر این، XC40 دارای سه گزینه چرخ الماس تراش است که در اندازه های 18، 19 و 20 اینچی موجود است.
اما فضای داخلی جایی است که پیشرفت‌های ولوو به دست می‌آید. صفحه نمایش به وضوح بالاتر و اندازه بزرگتر 11.2 اینچی افزایش یافته است. این جدیدترین رابط کاربری ولوو را اجرا می‌کند که خودروساز برای ناوبری سریع‌تر با ضربه‌های کمتر طراحی کرده است. Gemini گوگل به عنوان دستیار صوتی عمل می کند و از مغز بزرگ هوش مصنوعی خود برای برنامه ریزی مسیرها، یافتن مکان ها و مسیرهای انحرافی خاص و مدیریت پیام ها استفاده می کند. XC40 آن را با شارژر تلفن بی‌سیم بهبودیافته و راهکارهای ذخیره‌سازی هوشمند تکمیل می‌کند.
در مورد ایمنی چطور؟ به هر حال این یک ولوو است، خودروسازی که بیش از همه به ایمنی متعهد است (حداقل با توجه به شهرت آن). نگران نباشید، XC40 با نرم‌افزار و پلتفرم حسگر جدیدی که برای جلوگیری از برخورد بلادرنگ، فرمان خودکار اضطراری و ترمز خودکار اضطراری طراحی شده است، در این بخش پیشرفت می‌کند.
ارتقاء سنسور شامل رادارهای جلو و گوشه جدید، دوربین جلوی جدید، رادارهای گوشه عقب جدید، 12 سنسور جدید اولتراسونیک و دوربین های پارک جدید است. XC40 که در این مجموعه حسگر جدید پوشانده شده است، مجموعه ای از قابلیت های ایمنی جدید را دریافت می کند، از جمله هشدارهای جدید باز شدن درها که به سرنشینان قبل از عبور از درب دوچرخه سواران هشدار می دهد، کمک تغییر خط و پشتیبانی از مسیر صاف تر در رانندگی های طولانی، و دوربین اختیاری 3D/360 درجه برای ساده کردن مانور پارک و سرعت کم.
هدف نهایی ساخت XC40 بهتر است - XC40 ایمن تر و توانمندتر، که امیدواریم به آمار فروش بهتر و ماندگاری طولانی و مداوم برای SUV کوچک ولوو منجر شود.
آخیل کریشنان، سرپرست موقت سری 30 و 40 در ولوو کارز، در بیانیه‌ای می‌گوید: «با بهبود طراحی، فناوری و ویژگی‌های ایمنی XC40، ما بهترین نسخه XC40 را ایجاد کرده‌ایم. این مدل از قبل محبوب اکنون قرار است تا سال‌های آینده یکی از پرفروش‌ترین خودروهای ما باشد.»

title_en: 2028 Volvo XC40 First Look: Hello new tech, goodbye EV
title_fa: اولین نگاه ولوو XC40 2028: سلام فناوری جدید، خداحافظ EV
excerpt_en: Volvo refreshed the XC40, but it's sadly doing away with the all-electric EX40 in the US.
excerpt_fa: ولوو XC40 را به روز کرد، اما متأسفانه در حال حذف EX40 تمام الکتریکی در ایالات متحده است.
content_en:
2028 Volvo XC40 First Look: Hello new tech, goodbye EV
Volvo refreshed the XC40, but it's sadly doing away with the all-electric EX40 in the US.
Volvo is a brand traditionally known for its safety-minded station wagons and the Labrador Retrievers contained within, but lately it has well and truly embraced the SUV wave. While its midsize offering, the XC60, is its primary sales winner in the United States, the compact XC40 is the brand's third-best-selling model here, and second-highest internaionally.
The current-generation XC40 dates back to 2017, joined by the all-electric XC40 Recharge in 2019, which was rechristened in 2024 to become the EX40 to keep up with the company's evolving all-electric nomenclature. That branding includes the EX30, EX60, and the EX90.
For the 2028 model year, both the EX40 and XC40 are getting a major visual refresh plus an injection of extra tech into the software interface and active safety systems. That's the good news. The bad news? Starting in 2028, we'll only get half of that pairing.
A new look
The current-generation XC40 got a slight refresh in 2022, but looking back, you'd be forgiven for having a hard time telling the two versions apart, with a slightly reshaped nose and revised headlights.
For 2028, the revisions are a bit more significant, even if the overall shape of the car again remains largely the same. The front, though, is significantly revised. Where the front bumper formerly presented a face with numerous cut-outs and scalloped sections, now everything is far simpler.
It's a distinctly more modern look highlighted by the revised headlights. Yes, Volvo's trademark Thor's hammer design remains, but the various other lighting elements are now largely hidden, creating a stark effect.
Simpler designs
The hood and fenders have likewise been resculpted, and things out back have changed to match the revised front end, again all resulting in a cleaner design throughout. Cast a shadow over the new XC40, and you won't spot the differences, but in the daylight the net result is a distinctly more modern-looking SUV.
Over on the electric EX40, that machine gets all the same revisions. That means these two SUVs are nigh indistinguishable when sitting next to each other. Yes, the badging on the back is different, of course, but the bigger tell is the grille on the revised nose. The EX40's grille is a flat, body-colored panel, while the XC40's now contains an array of diagonal slashes meant to accentuate the Volvo logo and the arrow it's forever firing up and to the right.
New tech
Volvo retooled the interiors of the EX40 and XC40 as well, but the changes are even more subtle. The most notable is a new, larger screen that's been somewhat crudely grafted atop the center of the dashboard. Where the old display was nicely recessed between the tall central vents, fitting nicely in a recess in the dash, the new one stands outward, taller than the dash.
It's not a bad look, and the result is 11.2 inches of display real estate, up from the 9 inches the XC40 had before. The software running behind that screen has been updated as well, the latest flavor of Android Automotive that brings Google's Gemini to the party.
Gemini can handle changes to vehicle settings, control the infotainment experience and do everything else you'd expect your friendly local agentic instance to do — for better or worse. That means not only finding nearby restaurants but also getting summaries of their gluten-free offerings or vegetarian fare. Or, you can get route suggestions when you have a little extra time to kill and want to see some scenery on the way.
None of that, though, is exactly new. Indeed, Volvo added Gemini to most of its models earlier this year. Thankfully, the XC40's interior was already among the better-looking and feeling spaces in this segment, and that's still the case, now just with a bigger screen and some updated ambient lighting as well.
Enhanced safety
The biggest changes on the new EX40 and XC40 might be under the skin — or in some cases embedded within it. Volvo has outfitted these SUVs with an improved sensing package, including high-res cameras looking in every direction, ultrasonic sensors in the bumpers and updated radar.
This has a few immediate benefits, including the availability of a detailed, 3D view of the car that was previously restricted to Volvo's bigger, more expensive models. This also enables an automated lane-change feature in the Pilot Assist active safety system, which still includes an advanced, hands-on lane-keep system and adaptive cruise.
Those features are also said to be improved, with everything controlled by an updated central safety controller that has more processing power than before and is over-the-air updatable, meaning more advanced driver assistance features could be added down the road.
No details on which features might be coming and when, but don't hold your breath on hands-off driver systems like BMW's Highway Assistant or Tesla's Full Self-Driving. Volvo CEO Håkan Samuelsson has made it very clear that the company is in no rush to let drivers take their hands off the wheel.
Adios EX40
The final update is probably the saddest: While Volvo is updating both the EX40 and XC40 internationally, the United States will not be getting the updated battery-electric version. We'll only get the XC40 in B5 trim.
That means a 2.0-liter turbocharged four-cylinder engine that outputs 247 horsepower and 266 pound-feet of torque. It has an eight-speed automatic transmission and a small electric motor to help deliver a combined 27 mpg fuel efficiency.
The all-electric EX40 will live on internationally. Why not domestically? You can surely blame some combination of tepid sales and its foreign manufacture. That's a shame, especially since the smaller EX30 has also left American shores, but at least Volvo hasn't suffered Polestar's fate.

اولین نگاه ولوو XC40 2028: سلام فناوری جدید، خداحافظ EV
ولوو XC40 را به روز کرد، اما متأسفانه در حال حذف EX40 تمام الکتریکی در ایالات متحده است.
ولوو برندی است که به‌طور سنتی به خاطر استیشن واگن‌های ایمنی و لابرادور رتریورهای موجود در داخل شهرت دارد، اما اخیراً موج شاسی‌بلندها را به خوبی پذیرفته است. در حالی که مدل سایز متوسط ​​آن، XC60، برنده اصلی فروش آن در ایالات متحده است، XC40 جمع و جور سومین مدل پرفروش این برند در اینجا و دومین مدل پرفروش بین المللی است.
نسل کنونی XC40 به سال 2017 بازمی‌گردد، و در سال 2019 به XC40 Recharge تمام برقی پیوست که در سال 2024 مجدداً نامگذاری شد تا به EX40 تبدیل شود تا با نام‌گذاری تمام الکتریکی در حال تکامل شرکت همگام شود. این برند شامل EX30، EX60 و EX90 است.
برای مدل سال 2028، هر دو مدل EX40 و XC40 به‌روزرسانی بصری بزرگی به همراه تزریق فناوری اضافی به رابط نرم‌افزار و سیستم‌های ایمنی فعال دریافت می‌کنند. این خبر خوب است. خبر بد؟ از سال 2028، ما فقط نیمی از این جفت را خواهیم داشت.
یک نگاه جدید
نسل کنونی XC40 در سال 2022 کمی به‌روزرسانی شد، اما با نگاهی به گذشته، تشخیص این دو نسخه با دماغه‌ای کمی تغییر شکل‌یافته و چراغ‌های جلوی اصلاح‌شده دشوار است.
برای سال 2028، بازنگری ها کمی مهم تر هستند، حتی اگر شکل کلی خودرو دوباره تا حد زیادی یکسان باقی بماند. با این حال، قسمت جلو به طور قابل توجهی بازنگری شده است. در جایی که سپر جلو قبلاً چهره ای با برش های متعدد و بخش های اسکالوپ را نشان می داد، اکنون همه چیز بسیار ساده تر است.
این ظاهر کاملاً مدرن‌تر است که با چراغ‌های جلوی اصلاح‌شده برجسته شده است. بله، علامت تجاری ولوو، طرح چکش ثور باقی مانده است، اما عناصر مختلف نورپردازی دیگر اکنون تا حد زیادی پنهان شده‌اند و جلوه‌ای واضح ایجاد می‌کنند.
طرح های ساده تر
کاپوت و گلگیرها نیز به همین ترتیب تغییر شکل داده اند، و چیزهای بیرونی برای مطابقت با قسمت جلویی اصلاح شده تغییر کرده اند، که دوباره همه منجر به طراحی تمیزتر در سراسر آن شده است. بر روی XC40 جدید سایه بیندازید و تفاوت‌ها را متوجه نخواهید شد، اما در نور روز نتیجه خالص یک SUV کاملاً مدرن‌تر است.
در EX40 برقی، آن دستگاه تمام بازبینی‌های یکسانی را دریافت می‌کند. این بدان معناست که این دو شاسی بلند هنگام نشستن در کنار یکدیگر تقریباً قابل تشخیص نیستند. بله، نشان در پشت متفاوت است، البته، اما بزرگتر از مشبک روی دماغه اصلاح شده است. جلوپنجره EX40 یک پانل تخت و همرنگ بدنه است، در حالی که XC40 اکنون دارای مجموعه ای از خطوط مورب است که برای برجسته کردن آرم ولوو و پیکانی که برای همیشه به سمت راست و به سمت راست پرتاب می شود، قرار دارد.
تکنولوژی جدید
ولوو فضای داخلی EX40 و XC40 را نیز تغییر داد، اما تغییرات حتی ظریف‌تر هستند. قابل توجه ترین صفحه نمایش جدید و بزرگتر است که تا حدودی در بالای مرکز داشبورد پیوند زده شده است. در جایی که نمایشگر قدیمی به خوبی بین دریچه های مرتفع مرکزی فرو رفته بود و به خوبی در یک شکاف در داشبورد قرار می گرفت، نمایشگر جدید به سمت بیرون ایستاده بود، بلندتر از داشبورد.
ظاهر بدی نیست و نتیجه 11.2 اینچ صفحه نمایش واقعی است که نسبت به 9 اینچی XC40 قبلاً افزایش یافته است. نرم‌افزاری که پشت آن صفحه نمایش اجرا می‌شود نیز به‌روزرسانی شده است، آخرین مزیت Android Automotive که Gemini Google را به مهمانی می‌آورد.
Gemini می‌تواند تغییرات تنظیمات خودرو را کنترل کند، تجربه سرگرمی اطلاعاتی را کنترل کند و هر کار دیگری را که انتظار دارید از نمایندگی محلی دوستانه‌تان انجام دهد - چه بهتر یا چه بد. این بدان معناست که نه تنها رستوران های اطراف را پیدا کنید، بلکه خلاصه ای از پیشنهادات بدون گلوتن یا غذای گیاهی آنها را نیز دریافت کنید. یا، زمانی که کمی زمان بیشتری برای کشتن دارید و می‌خواهید مناظری را در راه ببینید، می‌توانید پیشنهادهای مسیر را دریافت کنید.
با این حال، هیچ یک از آن‌ها دقیقاً جدید نیستند. در واقع، ولوو Gemini را در اوایل سال جاری به اکثر مدل‌های خود اضافه کرد. خوشبختانه، فضای داخلی XC40 قبلاً در میان فضاهای زیباتر و احساسی در این بخش قرار داشت، و این هنوز هم همینطور است، اکنون فقط با یک صفحه نمایش بزرگتر و همچنین نور محیطی به روز شده.
ایمنی افزایش یافته است
بزرگترین تغییرات در EX40 و XC40 جدید ممکن است زیر پوست باشد - یا در برخی موارد درون آن تعبیه شده است. ولوو این خودروهای شاسی بلند را با یک بسته حسگر بهبودیافته، شامل دوربین‌های با رزولوشن بالا که در هر جهت نگاه می‌کنند، سنسورهای اولتراسونیک در سپرها و رادار به‌روز شده، تجهیز کرده است.
این چند مزیت فوری دارد، از جمله در دسترس بودن یک نمای سه بعدی دقیق از خودرو که قبلاً به مدل‌های بزرگتر و گران‌تر ولوو محدود می‌شد. این همچنین یک ویژگی تغییر خط خودکار را در سیستم ایمنی فعال Pilot Assist فعال می‌کند که همچنان شامل سیستم حفظ خطوط پیشرفته و عملی و کروز تطبیقی ​​است.
همچنین گفته می‌شود که این ویژگی‌ها بهبود یافته‌اند و همه چیز توسط یک کنترل‌کننده ایمنی مرکزی به‌روز شده کنترل می‌شود که قدرت پردازشی بیشتری نسبت به قبل دارد و قابلیت به‌روزرسانی از طریق هوا دارد، به این معنی که ویژگی‌های پیشرفته‌تر کمک راننده می‌تواند در جاده اضافه شود.
جزئیاتی در مورد اینکه چه ویژگی‌هایی ممکن است ارائه شوند و چه زمانی ارائه می‌شوند، وجود ندارد، اما در سیستم‌های راننده غیرفعال مانند دستیار بزرگراه BMW یا خودران کامل تسلا نفس خود را حبس نکنید. هاکان ساموئلسون، مدیر عامل ولوو، به صراحت اعلام کرده است که این شرکت عجله ای ندارد تا به رانندگان اجازه دهد دستان خود را از روی فرمان بردارند.
ادیوس EX40
به‌روزرسانی نهایی احتمالاً غم‌انگیزترین است: در حالی که ولوو هر دو EX40 و XC40 را در سطح بین‌المللی به‌روزرسانی می‌کند، ایالات متحده نسخه به‌روز شده باتری-الکتریکی را دریافت نخواهد کرد. ما فقط XC40 را در تریم B5 خواهیم داشت.
این به معنای یک موتور 2.0 لیتری توربوشارژ چهار سیلندر است که 247 اسب بخار قدرت و 266 پوند فوت گشتاور تولید می کند. این خودرو دارای یک گیربکس هشت سرعته اتوماتیک و یک موتور الکتریکی کوچک برای کمک به ارائه بازده سوخت ترکیبی 27 مایل بر گالن است.
EX40 تمام الکتریکی در سطح بین المللی زنده خواهد ماند. چرا داخلی نیست؟ مطمئناً می توانید ترکیبی از فروش کم و ساخت خارجی آن را مقصر بدانید. این مایه شرمساری است، به خصوص که EX30 کوچکتر نیز سواحل آمریکا را ترک کرده است، اما حداقل ولوو به سرنوشت Polestar دچار نشده است.
جمع بندی
بنابراین روزهای EX40 به شماره افتاده است و آن مدل پس از جریان فعلی به کدو تنبل تبدیل می شود ...
